transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Aaron Patel (Seabright Head of ML), Rhea Gupta (Seabright Eng Manager), Tom Martinez (Seabright Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick QBR, focus on costs, a couple reliability blips in May, want roadmap alignment and security docs.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today for the quarterly business review and health check, appreciate it. quick round of intros?
00:10 - Aaron Patel: Hi, Aaron here, head of ML at Seabright. we've been running prod recommendations and chat support through Redwood.
00:18 - Rhea Gupta: Rhea - engineering manager, I own infra and deployments, thanks.
00:22 - Tom Martinez: Tom, security lead - I'll ask the usual compliance Qs.
00:26 - Liam O'Connor: Liam from Redwood, I'll handle the performance questions today.
00:30 - Maya Chen: Great, we'll walk through usage trends, cost, reliability incidents, then roadmap and next steps.

02:05 - Maya Chen: Quick data point from our side - your monthly tokens have increased ~28% month-over-month, mostly embeddings and chat. is that expected?
02:18 - Aaron Patel: Yeah, embeddings for search expansion went up after we rolled the sitewide reindex in late April. chat usage also spiked during the marketing campaign in mid-May.
02:30 - Rhea Gupta: The spike's fine but we're worried about unit cost, the bill jump was bigger than we anticipated. can you help explain per-route costs?
02:42 - Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll send the per-route breakdown; looks like the customer-facing chat route is the main driver. we can look at batching/response length and also model choice.

05:00 - Liam O'Connor: On performance, we saw two latency incidents in May: one at 2026-05-12 03:22 UTC where p95 went to ~2.1s and another on 2026-05-27 with a short spike to 3.6s. both recovered in under 5 minutes. these were on hosted capacity during a regional network blip and a heavy burst.
05:30 - Rhea Gupta: For us, p95 in the 800-900ms range is the bar. those spikes did surface as degraded UX. are there guardrails?
05:40 - Liam O'Connor: Yes - we recommend setting a route-level failover to your dedicated pool or a cheaper compact model for fallback, and enable autoscale buffer on Dedicated. also prefix caching can avoid repeated KV cache repopulation for common prompts.
06:10 - Tom Martinez: On the security side, we had a question about KMS - are keys customer-managed for Private? and what about log retention?
06:22 - Sofia Alvarez: For Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; for Dedicated we have encryption at rest by default and can integrate with your KMS for key rotation. log retention is configurable, and we can provide audit logs for the last 90 days, extended retention is an add-on.

08:50 - Aaron Patel: We're evaluating Dedicated capacity - we want predictable throughput and less noisy neighbor risk. cost-wise, how should we think about break-even versus hosted?
09:05 - Maya Chen: Generally Dedicated makes sense when you have sustained throughput; the break-even depends on your token volume and latency SLOs. we'll run a modeled comparison and include the reserved commit option.
09:20 - Rhea Gupta: Do you have any quantization or faster variants that preserve quality? we've been experimenting with 4-bit quantized models for embeddings.
09:30 - Liam O'Connor: We recommend the quantized variants for large batch embedding jobs; for chat we can evaluate mixed precision. there are performance profiles we can share — sometimes quality regressions happen, so we tie eval sets to monitor regressions.

12:00 - Aaron Patel: Speaking of regressions, we've seen a slight dip in intent classification accuracy after the model upgrade in April. not huge but measurable. how do we trace that?
12:18 - Liam O'Connor: We can run A/B rollouts and surface per-prompt eval results in Redwood Console. also we'll link the evals to your success criteria and set regression alerts. if needed, we can pin to the previous model until it's addressed.

15:10 - Tom Martinez: One compliance ask — can you share SOC2 and SSO integration docs? also what about IP retention policies if we do Private?
15:25 - Sofia Alvarez: We'll share the SOC2 summary and the SSO/SAML guide. Private gives you control over data residency and retention; we can outline options in the SOC/contract addendum.

18:40 - Rhea Gupta: On the roadmap, any upcoming features we should expect that can reduce cost?
18:50 - Maya Chen: We're rolling out smarter batching heuristics and more aggressive prefix caching later this quarter, plus Optimize will push model & quantization recommendations per-workload. those should reduce unit cost for steady workloads.

21:00 - Aaron Patel: Can we get a real example of cost savings if we switch embedding bulk jobs to a quantized pipeline? a rough delta would help justify infra changes.
21:10 - Maya Chen: Yes — we'll provide a modeled delta with sample jobs included.

24:00 - Liam O'Connor: Quick note on dedicated benchmarks — we'll run throughput tests with 4k context, report p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for batch sizes 1, 8, 32; that should help you pick reserved capacity.

27:30 - Rhea Gupta: For rollout, we have a canary window policy and want automated rollback if latency > 1.5s or error rate > 0.5%. can Redwood support that?
27:45 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. we can wire the thresholds to your alerting and do automatic route-level fallback.

30:00 - Tom Martinez: A couple nitty-gritty security Qs: is the audit log immutable? who has access in Redwood Console?
30:12 - Sofia Alvarez: Audit logs are tamper-evident and we can set RBAC so only designated admins see them. we'll share a sample RBAC matrix for your security review.

33:40 - Aaron Patel: Ok, let's recap priorities: 1) cost deep-dive for May spike, 2) Dedicated benchmark, 3) SOC2 & SSO docs, 4) list of top prompts and success metrics for evals.
33:58 - Maya Chen: yep that's the plan — I'll send the cost dashboard and proposed benchmark schedule.

35:10 - Rhea Gupta: one more thing — do you offer per-route throttling or quota controls we can use to limit bursts from the marketing campaign?
35:22 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have per-route quota and rate limiting, plus dynamic throttles. we can set those now or set suggestions via Optimize.

38:00 - Maya Chen: Next steps and owners — will capture in the notes and follow up. anything else from Seabright?
38:10 - Aaron Patel: no, that covers it. thanks.
38:15 - Tom Martinez: thanks all.

Recap / Closing (automated):
00:00-45:00 - QBR focused on usage growth (embeddings & chat), cost spike in May, two short latency incidents on hosted, interest in Dedicated capacity, security documentation request (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and action items to run benchmarks and share dashboards.

Final words:
44:30 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.
44:45 - Sofia Alvarez: I'll drop SOC2 + SSO steps in the thread.
44:50 - Meeting ended.
